title: Pinned release manifest: explicit compatibility tiers for prompts, outputs, and runtime parameters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a canonical 'pinned release manifest' artifact and validation process that explicitly declares backward-compatibility guarantees for any model version that customers can pin. The manifest will specify three compatibility dimensions: prompt schema (allowed input shapes and tokenization expectations), output shape and stability (field names, types, ordering, structural constraints), and runtime parameter semantics (temperature, max_tokens, stop tokens, and any vendor/model-specific flags). The goal is to give customers deterministic expectations for pinned versions and enable automated checks during onboarding and rollout. This ticket covers the manifest schema, the CLI/CI validator used by model-onboarding, and a lightweight conformance test harness for Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema v1 defined and documented with examples for prompt, output, and parameter compatibility tiers
CLI validator implemented that fails onboarding if manifest fields are missing or violate schema
Conformance test harness (integration test) can run against a candidate model and emit a pass/fail matrix for each compatibility dimension
Onboarding checklist updated to require manifest and CI badge before marking model 'pinnable' in the catalog
Backward-compatibility guarantees surfaced in the model catalog UI for pinned versions
decisions: Use three-tier compatibility levels: strict, tolerant, and evolutionary. Strict = exact field and tokenization parity; Tolerant = stable semantics but allowed ordering/optional fields; Evolutionary = may add non-breaking fields with explicit migration notes
Manifest will be JSON Schema-compatible but remain a flat key/value first-class artifact to simplify storage and diffing
Validator will run locally (cli) and in CI; conformance harness will be optional in early onboarding but required for release to 'pinned' state
We will treat tokenizer changes as a major compatibility break unless remapped token offsets are provided by model owners
rollout_plan: Week 0: proto-schema drafted, share with PM and Design for feedback
Week 1: implement CLI validator and sample manifests for two internal models
Week 2: integrate conformance tests into onboarding pipeline and gate 'pinnable' flag behind badge
Week 3: update model catalog to display manifest summary and compatibility tier
Week 4: run smoke migration for 3 existing pinned candidates and gather runtime telemetry
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest schema parsing and validator edge-cases
Integration tests: run conformance harness against 'redwood-rl-fun' and 'open-m-chat' internal test models
Chaos tests: simulate tokenization divergence and verify validator flags break
E2E: onboarding pipeline must fail when manifest absent; succeed when present and conformance pass

notes: Prefer explicit 'breaking_change' boolean in manifest entries to avoid ambiguous semantics
Consider providing a mapping layer for token offsets to support best-effort tokenizer changes
We may extend manifest with perf annotations (p50/p95 token latency at common batch sizes) in a later iteration
Keep manifest human-readable and reviewable during model PRs to simplify audits
